title: Docs gallery: the basic-tooltip and basic-hover-card entries render a completely blank tile — each authors a key its renderer never reads
body:
Measured while implementing #4616 (the gallery registration widening). Filed unassigned; **not** fixed there — both types are registered by `@object-ui/components` and neither tile is a registration failure, so they fall outside that card's scope. Duplicate-searched (keyword + the two entry paths + `renderChildren`): no open issue covers it.

## The defect

Rendering all 423 catalog entries the way `SchemaThumbnail` renders them, these two produce **no DOM of their own at all** — the harness wrapper is empty:

```
  body > div > div.group/sidebar-wrapper > div.w-full.p-4    (nothing inside)
```

They are not red tiles, so no OBJUI-001 sweep would ever notice them; they are blank cards on a published page. Two different causes, same result.

### 1. `components-overlay-tooltip/basic-tooltip`

The entry authors its trigger under `children`:

```json
{
  "type": "tooltip",
  "content": "Helpful information",
  "children": [ { "type": "button", "label": "Hover me" } ]
}
```

`packages/components/src/renderers/overlay/tooltip.tsx` reads `schema.trigger` and `schema.body` and never looks at `children`, so `TooltipTrigger asChild` gets nothing and the tile is empty. The registry meta for the type lists `trigger` and `body` as its slots, so the renderer is the one following the declared surface here.

### 2. `components-overlay-hover-card/basic-hover-card`

Both slots author `value` where the text renderer reads `content`:

```json
{
  "type": "hover-card",
  "trigger": { "type": "text", "value": "Hover over me" },
  "content": { "type": "text", "value": "This is the hover card content" }
}
```

`packages/components/src/renderers/basic/text.tsx` renders `schema.content`; `value` is not a key it reads, so both nodes render empty and the trigger has nothing to clone.

## Why this is worth a card rather than a two-line patch

Both are one-key corrections, but the class is the interesting part: nothing rejects an authored key the renderer does not read. A schema naming `children` where the component declares `trigger`, or `value` where it declares `content`, publishes clean and renders blank — which is precisely the failure mode AI-authored metadata produces most often, and the catalog is the corpus those tools retrieve from. Worth deciding whether unknown keys on a registered type should be a publish-time rejection rather than silence.

Both entries are named as explicit exclusions, with this issue number, in `examples/schema-catalog/test/catalog-gallery-render.test.tsx` — the non-vacuity control there ("the tile drew something of its own") is what surfaced them, and removing the exclusions is the natural last step of fixing this.

Refs #4616, PR #4615.
